column2: Ted Dreier leaves for the East on college business
Bob Wunsch returns after a week with his mother in Monroe (Louisiana)
Maria Hansgirg returns after two weeks at the Biltmore Hospital in Asheville
Josef Albers speaks to the students of the Lawrenceville School
Em and Mac Wood drive to Delray Beach (Florida) until the spring quarter
The Board of Fellows announces the appointment of Max Dehn (visiting professor of mathematics) and David Corkran (history, winter and spring)
Josef Albers speaks to the art section of the Association of Private Schools at the Museum of Modern Art

Recent visitors: Mr. and Mrs. Siegfried Schwarz, friends of the Jalowetzes (Schwarz is a candidate for the position in economics and as an assistant in the office), Betty Rhodes (Cleveland), Lieutenant Bill Berry for the weekend
The final winter quarter schedule goes into effect
Marriage of Margaret Greene and Lieutenant Donald Edward Pickett at the home of the bride's mother
Josef Albers returns to campus (Wednesday or Thursday); visitors to his classes on Thursday and Friday
Trudi Straus leaves for Baltimore to join Erwin Straus for the week
Janie and Lieutenant Fred Stone arrive for four days with Mrs. Annette Stone and their friends at the college
Lake Eden freezes hard enough for skating: two days of skating, the college's main amusement
Arrival of Mr. and Mrs. Milton Rose (Winston-Salem), attorney for the Whitney Foundation; departure Wednesday morning for Tryon
Janie and Fred Stone leave for Tampa, where Fred will be stationed for several months
The Roses leave for Tryon
Dr. Else Toller spends the evening at the college
The Board of Fellows announces the appointment of Siegfried Schwarz as instructor in economics; expected to arrive at the end of the week
Betty Kelley and Jane Slater pass their trial oral and written examinations for graduation
Mrs. David Corkran and her three children (David, John, Robert) arrive at Lake Eden
Mr. and Mrs. Siegfried Schwarz drive in from New York
Helen Rosenbluth arrives and starts as Fritz Hansgirg's secretary
Other visitors of the week: Frederic Cohen (second summer institute, with the Music Institute Corporation of New York), Paul Beidler, Mr. and Mrs. Harold Bush-Brown
Bobbie Dreier leaves by train for New York and New England
Mrs. Mary Gregory, Molly's mother, arrives from Tennessee; leaves on Thursday for Wenham (Massachusetts)
Ted Dreier leaves for Florida, for the funeral of his aunt Mrs. Raymond Robins
Kenneth Kurtz arrives; he leaves on Tuesday for Yale to resume his studies in literature
Marriage of Peggy Emery and Kenneth Kurtz in Asheville
Trudi Straus leaves for Baltimore; concert at St. John's College on March 4; back March 6
Max Paul appointed head of the fire prevention and firefighting organization
Kenneth Kurtz leaves for Yale
Student weavings included in an exhibition of modern textiles at Skidmore College
Trudi Straus returns to Lake Eden
Lecture tour by Dr. Samuel Guy Inman (State Department adviser on Latin America) at twenty-one North Carolina institutions, March 8-22, including a visit to the college
Bobbie and Ted Dreier guests of Mr. and Mrs. Theodore Rondthaler in Clemmons
The Dreiers visit Chapel Hill
Vaclav Vytlacil, head of the art department of Queens College, arrives to give the art orals of Marilyn Bauer and Jane Slater; guest of the college until Saturday afternoon
Departure of Vaclav Vytlacil
Mendez Marks, now at the New Yorker, arrives on Easter morning, his first visit since he left in spring 1942
Other visitors: Sergeant and Mrs. Libert Ehrman (Irma Ehrman's family), Florence Schust, a New York architect, for several days
Mrs. Walter Boyden arrives for two weeks
Josef Albers leaves for New York to meet the future faculty of the 1945 Summer Art Institute
Edward Lowinsky leaves for Boston on a business trip for the college
Dr. Earl Newcomer expected for the weekend
Earl Newcomer leads a nature walk on the college lands
Mrs. Max Dehn arrives to join her husband
Ted Dreier due to leave for Chicago on a business trip
Bob Wunsch chairs the panel “Educational Values in Dramatics” at the state drama festival (with Paul Green, Betty Smith, A. T. West)
Evsey Domar goes back to Washington after several days at the college
The students perform Tennessee Williams's “Landscape with Figures” at the festival
Ted Dreier leaves for Chicago on a business trip
Mrs. Max Dehn goes back to Chicago
Mary Rice Marshall goes back to Washington (Department of Justice) after two weeks with her mother
Trudi Straus returns after her concerts with the North Carolina Symphony Orchestra
Josef Albers returns from New York, where he assembled the faculty of the 1945 Summer Art Institute
Edward Lowinsky returns from Boston (preparations for the 1945 Summer Music Institute)
Marriage of Margaret Macdonald Clapp and Midshipman Harry Orland King Jr.
Mrs. Claire McCanna, Alice's mother, visiting
Special faculty meeting in the Music Roundhouse: Betty Kelley, the last student from the Blue Ridge days, receives her diploma (dramatic literature, acting, playwriting)
Betty Kelley goes home on vacation to Fulton (Kentucky)
Ted Dreier returns after a ten-day business trip (Chicago, New York, Washington)
Mr. and Mrs. Theodore Rondthaler expected April 27 to 29

Work program: wood and the bottom of the coal pile for the furnaces in cold weather; framing of the Service Building completed despite the rain; stone walls of a culvert near Roadside Cottage (Paul Beidler); volunteers to address 3500 envelopes for the institute bulletins
Ann and Fred Mangold arrive from Mexico City
Elena Gomez, the new secretary, arrives from New York and starts in the office of the art and music institutes
Walter Gropius and John E. Burchard, members of the Advisory Council, expected for the weekend
Ted Marburg and Lee Shames spend Saturday evening and Sunday at Lake Eden
The first three hundred copies of the 1945 Summer Music Institute bulletin come off the press
Helen Wright Marden leaves for a two-week vacation in Boston
Visitors of the week: Mrs. Emma Hoffman, Mrs. Anna D. Jamieson (Advisory Council), Fred Mangold, Mendez Marks, Ira De A. Reid, Theodore Rondthaler, Dr. Else Toller
Max Dehn leaves for Washington; back at the end of the week
Lieutenant William C. Berry, pilot of a B-25, reported missing during an air attack on the Kuril Islands
Herbert Miller, chairman of the price control information panel (OPA) for Black Mountain, Swannanoa, and Oteen, speaks on price control at the Black Mountain high school assembly
Work starts on the two new music practice rooms; at the Service Building, hardwood floor begun, plumbing and wiring finished
Farm: eighteen piglets; twenty acres of alfalfa and barley mowed, ten acres of silage corn planted, sweet corn, peas, onions, tomatoes, leeks; ground prepared for a thousand plants; soybean plowing

Visitors of the week: Captain Joseph W. Jailer, Mrs. Todd Dabney, Mrs. Wallace Gill, Dr. C. L. Siegel, Mrs. Marli Ehrman and her son, Lieutenant and Mrs. Don Kelley, Thaddeus Malinowski, Dr. Paul Schwartzkopf
Ted, Bobbie, and Liddie Dreier leave by train for Lake George (New York)
Siegfried Schwarz and his wife leave for New York on college business
Mrs. Theodore Rondthaler arrives from Winston-Salem; she starts in the business office the next day
Mrs. Norton Garth (Coral Gables) expected for two or three days
Peggy Kurtz leaves the college to join Kenneth Kurtz in New Haven
Lieutenant and Mrs. Don Kelley go back to Washington after two weeks: they took part in the activities and are thinking of founding a school after the war
Soybeans sown
Fernando Leon, a student from 1939 to 1942, visiting; he has just received his master's degree in engineering in Detroit
First of the two summer concerts by the faculty of the Summer Music Institute, organized by the Hendersonville Music Club and the chamber of commerce
Music Institute concert: Franck, Debussy, Ravel, Fauré, Saint-Saëns, Brahms
Second summer concert by the Summer Music Institute faculty in Hendersonville
Frances Snow Drinker, flutist of the Music Institute, leaves the college
Harriett Engelhardt, a former student, killed in a jeep accident near Munich

Rondthaler and Mrs. Rondthaler drive Hazel, Max Dehn, and Elaine Schmitt to the Asheville train; impromptu student meeting in the railroad car: Dehn elected a member of the student body, chaired by Hank Bergman, the new moderator
Molly Gregory hands over the farm accounts to Lore Kadden and leaves with Anni and Josef Albers, behind the Mortons, for Winston-Salem
Alice Stieglitz was to fly to New York, but the flight is canceled; Harry Weitzer feverish in the infirmary
The Asheville airport finds a seat for Alice Stieglitz on the direct flight
Group supper in front of the South Lodge fireplace, songs by Walcott and Wallen
Harry Weitzer leaves on the night train, accompanied by Anne Mayer and Estelle Levi; the Hansgirgs leave by car
Departure of Halsie Wright Marden (to join Bob, back from overseas) and of Roxane Dinkowitz
Billie Furman, a friend of Lore Kadden, back from Guam, arrives for the holidays
Dr. and Mrs. Miller leave for Richmond and Washington

Christmas shopping in Asheville in the snow (Lowinsky, Wallen, Daisy Walcott, Bobbie Rondthaler, Mrs. Penley, Mrs. Rondthaler); the car is left at the bottom of the hill on the ice, rides back by truck, taxi, and train
